title: Regularized Principal Component Analysis for Hybrid Data
text: ReMPCA R package designed extend Principal Component Analysis (PCA) complex, high-dimensional datasets—including curves, images, functional, regular data. integrating multiple data types within single framework, ReMPCA captures intricate relationships across variables domains, making ideal tool structured data analysis fields like imaging, signal processing, functional data analysis. Unlike traditional PCA methods, ReMPCA offers flexible, fine-grained control one- two-way regularization. Users can independently apply smoothing sparsity different data components, tailored regularization parameters across functional regular sections. Built enhanced power algorithm, package dynamically refines components quantifies explained variance, delivering powerful unified solution extracting meaningful structure hybrid datasets. Implementing varied penalties uu vv improves accuracy. shown Figure , noisy chessboard, applying power algorithm customized penalties, smoothness group lasso, enforces step-function structure uu vv, refining vectors yielding reconstruction close true chessboard. importantly, regularizing directions simultaneously effective separate one-way penalties, better preserving data’s true structure.

title: Regularized Principal Component Analysis for Hybrid Data
text: following example demonstrates generate q hybrid data (regular functional) construct input objects required running ReMPCA:
code: library(ReMPCA) set.seed(123)  # Create a common left singular vector u (length 150), with sparsity in the first half x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 150) u <- sin(x) u[1:75] <- 0  ### Construct 4 variables with different characteristics  # Variable 1: Sparse right singular vector m1 <- 20 v1 <- rnorm(m1, sd = 0.8) v1[sample(1:m1, 5)] <- v1[sample(1:m1, 5)] * 1e-2 + rnorm(5, sd = 0.01) X1 <- outer(u, v1) + rnorm(150 * m1, sd = 0.03)  # Variable 2: Piecewise smooth right singular vector (functional) x2 <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 40) v2 <- cos(2 * x2) v2[21:40] <- 0  # Create piecewise structure X2 <- outer(u, v2) + rnorm(150 * 40, sd = 0.5)  # Variable 3: Smooth right singular vector (functional) m3 <- 30 x3 <- seq(0, pi, length.out = m3) v3 <- sin(x3) X3 <- outer(u, v3) + rnorm(150 * m3, sd = 0.2)  # Variable 4: Random structure m4 <- 10 v4 <- rnorm(m4) X4 <- outer(u, v4) + rnorm(150 * m4, sd = 0.05)  # Combine all variables into a single matrix (optional, not used directly) X <- cbind(X1, X2, X3, X4)  ### Create hybrid data objects  # Regular data (RD) object rd_object1 <- rdClass(   data = as.matrix(X1),   Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(1, 19, length.out = 10)) )  # Functional data (FD) objects fd_object2 <- fdClass(   data = as.matrix(X2),   argval = NULL,   Smoothing_parameter = NULL,   Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0, 39, length.out = 20)) )  fd_object3 <- fdClass(   data = as.matrix(X3),   argval = NULL,   Smoothing_parameter = NULL,   Sparsity_parameter = 0 )  # Another regular data object rd_object4 <- rdClass(   data = as.matrix(X4),   Sparsity_parameter = 0 )  # Combine all objects into a hybrid data structure hd_list <- list(rd_object1, fd_object2, fd_object3, rd_object4) object_list <- hdClass(   hdlist = hd_list,   argval = NULL,   Smoothing_parameter = NULL,   Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0, 149, length.out = 20)) )  # Plot the data par(mfrow = c(2, 4), pin = c(1, 1), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2), pty = "s")  # Variable 1: Regular matplot(v1, type = 'p', pch = 16, main = 'v1, Regular')  abline(h = 0, col = 'red', lty = 2) image(t(X1), main = 'X1, Regular')  # Variable 2: Functional matplot(svd(X2)$v[,1], type = 'l', main = 'v2, Functional')  abline(h = 0, col = 'red', lty = 2) image(t(X2), main = 'X2, Functional')  # Variable 3: Functional matplot(svd(X3)$v[,1], type = 'l', main = 'v3, Functional') image(t(X3), main = 'X3, Functional')  # Variable 4: Regular matplot(v4, type = 'p', pch = 16, main = 'v4, Regular') image(t(X4), main = 'X4, Regular')

title: Functional Data Class — fdClass
text: fdClass class represents element functional data. Data objects constructed using matrices, columns represent grid points (user-defined NULL) rows represent observations. Users can assign smoothing sparsity parameters. smoothing parameter set zero, smoothing applied. Otherwise, users can specify fixed smoothing value provide vector values, optimized using generalized cross-validation (GCV).

title: Functional Data Class — fdClass
text: data matrix representing data, rows indicating observations columns representing grid points. argval vector grid points, assigns grid points columns, length equal number columns data. NULL, grid points automatically assigned 0 1. Smoothing_parameter : Smoothing parameter columns. can : fixed number representing smoothing parameter. vector numerical values, undergo generalized cross-validation (GCV) determine optimal value. Set 0 smoothing. NULL, analyzes sequence 2^seq(-30, 5, length.= 10) attempts tune . Sparsity_parameter fixed number representing level sparsity columns, vector numerical values undergo cross-validation (CV) determine optimal value. sparsity, set 0. NULL, sparsity parameter tuned automatically.

title: ReMPCA 0.1.0
text: Row-sparsity cross-validation now predicts held-columns least-squares loadings v = X'u / ||u||^2, manuscript. Previously scores normalized, mis-scaled CV error led -sparse row scores whenever several row-sparsity levels compared. ReMPCA() num_pcs > 1 now deflates data estimated regularized component (Algorithm 1 accompanying paper) instead leading unregularized singular component. Unpenalized fits unchanged. VarianceExplained now computed estimated (regularized) loadings rather unregularized singular vectors. one-standard-error rule loading sparsity now uses standard error K-fold CV mean (previously used standard deviation fold errors), row-sparsity tuning now honours cv.pick tuning orders (hard-coded "min" tuning_order = "Sparsity"). Cross-validation longer resets user’s random number generator (set.seed() inside package); folds still use fixed internal seed, results unchanged reproducible. Empty folds (many folds data size) longer produce NA indices. $ methods classes gave error inside error message (sprintf() missing argument). [.hdClass returned data frame labelled hdClass; now returns valid hdClass matrix. [.imgClass collapsed selected images one row; *.imgClass returned list-matrix; plot.imgClass() displayed images scrambled (vectorized row-wise rebuilt column-wise) longer waits input non-interactive sessions. [.fdClass [.rdClass keep matrix structure subset grid points columns. Internal fixes roughness-matrix bookkeeping (opt_alpha_Omega_*) affect fitted values. Unknown sparse_tuning_type, smoothness_type, tuning_order, cv.pick values now give informative error.

title: ReMPCA 0.1.0
text: New argument verbose ReMPCA(); progress messages can suppressed. Plot functions restore user’s graphical parameters exit. parallel = TRUE, internal cluster uses min(6, detectCores()) workers. energydata data set now contains object named energydata (previously appliance_dat) xz-compressed; read.data() can load . Documentation: return values runnable examples exported functions, references, test suite. Reproducibility scripts bike-sharing appliances-energy applications inst/reproducibility now use packaged data, can run working directory, save manuscript figures.
